—Transplant our Magic Circuits into each other?

Magic Circuits are a mage's second, artificial nervous system—the very substance of what they are.

They are the mechanism by which a mage uses the energy within to act upon the energy of the greater world.

A living inheritance, accumulated over generations so that some future descendant, should they ever *reach* the ultimate mystery, will possess the foundation necessary to realize its theory.

One might call them blood and bone, made richer and stronger through accumulation.

“*Nimm an, ohne anderer Meinung zu sein, ohne zu fallen.*

“*Es nimmt an, ohne zu fürchten, ohne zu zweifeln.*

“*Sieg im Freund, der auf eine Reise entfernt geht.*”

Small into great, great into small; from the joined wings, a beginning.

My eyelids feel sewn shut.

The sense of smell through which I perceived Tohsaka grows dull. My tongue discovers an empty flavor.

The sensation of my body slips out of alignment. I can no longer tell whether I am sitting or standing.

In exchange, the place where Tohsaka's skin touches mine burns with impossible heat. I cannot distinguish my own pulse from her rhythm.

An illusory pain: someone is gripping my heart.

An illusory experience: I am gripping someone else's.

I move my fingers, seeking the sensation of the palm transmitted to me—

“…………Nn!”

My ears still function. I hear the voice.

No—my body has become indistinct. I cannot tell whether the body is mine or whether the sound I just heard was Tohsaka's voice.

“Hah… ngh………hah…”

…Each breath that escapes is painfully strained.

Though I know it is not my own breathing I hear, I cannot help listening.

The rebuke comes from inside me.

I try to ask what is happening—what any of this means.

体が紙になって、パタパタと折りたたまれていくような感覚。
ゆっくりと、丁寧に仕舞われていく。だが外界の時間は止まっているため、外から見れば光速の出来事だろう。

The instant I hear that much, I abruptly lose myself.

My body becomes a sheet of paper, folded smaller and smaller.

Slowly, carefully, I am put away. Yet time in the outer world has stopped, so from without the event must occur at the speed of light.

There is no end to the folding, no limit to the reduction. Any plane, however vast, can only be folded so many times, yet I continue closing inward upon myself.

My vision turns blue. The world before I was folded had been red.

浮いている。
落下しているのに浮遊しており、かつ、世界は高速で過ぎ去っていく。
その、高速と停止の混ざり合った世界に慣れようと手を伸ばそうとし、

—I am floating.

I fall and float at once, while the world streams past at tremendous speed.

I try to reach out, hoping to accustom myself to this world where motion and stillness commingle—

pages.ja:
あ。
そもそも、腕なんてとっくに折りたたまれているのでない事に気が付いた。
それは困る。余分なもの、此処では無くてもいいものを削られてきたが、手足がないのは考え物だ。なにしろ自分を認識できない。
ので、まずやるべき事は、世界の確認ではなく、自己フォルムの想定だった。

—Ah.

I realize that my arms were folded away long ago and no longer exist.

That is a problem. Everything unnecessary—everything I do not need here—has been stripped from me, but without limbs, I cannot even recognize myself.

Therefore my first task is not to examine the world, but to imagine a form for myself.

pages.ja:
両手を握る。
己を、仮定ではあるが、確かに認識した。
上も下もない。空も大地もない。青い天球に浮かんでいる。
静かだ。音の話ではなく、カタチそのものが静かで、完結している。

pages.en:
I clench both hands.

Though the form is hypothetical, I can now perceive myself with certainty.

There is neither above nor below, neither sky nor earth. I float within a blue celestial sphere.

It is quiet—not in sound, but in form. Complete and perfectly still.

pages.ja:
時間は外で回っている。
外はすべて碧い海で満たされている。
天球の中には何もない。
つまり
碧い海にとって、この天球こそが空だった。

pages.en:
Time moves outside it.

Everything beyond is filled by an azure sea.

Within the celestial sphere, there is nothing.

In other words—to that blue sea, the sphere itself is the sky.

pages.ja:
世界の卵。
この天球がカラによって覆われているのか。
それとも内と外があべこべになっているのか。
無から生じた全か、全からはみ出した無か。
逆しまなまま、天球は回り続ける。

pages.en:
The egg of the world.

Is this celestial sphere enclosed within a shell?

Or have inside and outside been reversed?

Is it everything born from nothing, or the nothing that overflowed from everything?

Inversion unresolved, the sphere continues to turn.

pages.ja:
それは回り続けた時間。
永い年月をかけて形を得た無形。
何一つ同じ形はなく、何一つ違う命はない。
全てに共通する事象。
同じ形のものが群がって、まったく違う法則を形づくる。

pages.en:
It is time that has continued turning.

The immaterial given form across countless years.

No two shapes are the same, yet no life among them is different.

A phenomenon common to them all.

Things of the same form gather together and construct entirely different laws.

pages.ja:
一つ一つの希少な要因が、
一つ一つの偉大な結果を表している。
美しい。まるで、海を渡る魚のようだ。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
Each singular cause manifests a singular, magnificent result.

—Beautiful. Like fish crossing the sea.

pages.ja:
完成された世界には何の意志も存在しない。
存続も防衛も、共生も敵対も導き出さない。
ここは訪れた者を意図とするもの。
我が搾取する為に落ちた異物であるのなら。
それらは、当然のように応えるだろう。

No will exists within this completed world.

It seeks neither continuance nor defense, neither coexistence nor enmity.

This place takes as its purpose the one who visits it.

If I am foreign matter fallen here to harvest it, then they will answer that purpose as naturally as breathing.

だが、注意しなくてはいけないのは、

The aggregate that is the Crest gathers up the intruder's intent.

But there is something I must remember—

Inversion.

A vision.

A hidden past that does not belong to me passes through.

ある人物との別れの朝。戦いが始まるからと、冬木を離れた別荘に置いて行かれた余人の記憶。

I see an old memory.

The morning she parted from a certain person. The memory of another, left behind in a villa beyond Fuyuki because a war was about to begin.

pages.ja:
注意しなくてはいけないのは。
どのような意図による反応であれ。
ソレらが行う過程は、人識にとって、神罰以外の何物でもないという事。

—What I must remember—

is that whatever intention they may answer,

the process by which they answer it can be nothing but divine punishment to human perception.

Though this body requires neither eyes nor brain, vertigo seizes me.

Information streams past.

I pass through an old memory.

The morning she parted from a certain person.

The memory of another, watching them leave in the knowledge that their hands would never meet again.

The lines of the Magic Crest swim around me.

They circle and circle, probing the morsel that has appeared among them.

…There is nothing I can do.

From the beginning, prey has no choices to make.

Only by observing everything and accepting it can I produce any result at all.

Persons: two.

Season: winter.

Designation: farewell.

墓標の前に佇む少女。

A bouquet laid in offering.

A girl standing before a gravestone.

Behind her, a priest tall enough to loom over everything.

There are no words.

On this day too, the girl remains strong and seals away her grief.

全身を絞り上げる螺旋の刃。
悪質なトラツグミに似ている。
刻印の移植が、始まった。

pages.en:
Foreign matter introduced.

A spiraling blade wrings my entire body dry.

It resembles some malicious thrush.

The transplantation of the Crest has begun.

pages.ja:
凄惨な事実を観測する。
幸い、痛みを感じる機能は折りたたまれている。
他人事のように施錠され、緊縛され、分断され、解体され、圧縮され、弄ばれる自分を眺める。

I observe the grisly reality as an image.

Fortunately, the part of me capable of feeling pain has already been folded away.

As though it concerns someone else, I watch myself locked, bound, divided, dismantled, compressed, and toyed with.

Flesh is remarkably easy to mince.

Bone is comparatively easy to shave away.

In the end, nothing remains but a soul that can be made to suffer forever.

pages.ja:
片手だけ、虫の腕になった
みたいに、
気持ち、悪い。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
As though one of my hands

has become the limb of an insect—

revolting.

これは彼女の苦痛でもある。
いつか聞いた、魔術刻印を宿す痛み。
尊敬する。
あいつはこんな不快感を、おそらくはこれより数倍のおぞましさを体に棲まわせて、鮮やかに笑うのだ。
気持ちの悪さなどない。
それを思えば、何を恐れる事があるだろう。

This pain belongs to her as well.

The agony of bearing a Magic Crest—something I once heard her describe.

I admire her.

She carries this horror within her body—something surely many times worse than what I feel—and smiles with radiant ease.

The disgust vanishes.

When I think of her, what is there left to fear?

I touch something deeper than all the rest.

Among memories filled with farewells, there was one—

one encounter bright enough to scorch her heart.

Someone was running across the schoolyard.

The high jump.

Again and again, he ran toward the bar.

そんな事に意味があるのかと。
何か裏切られたような、尊いものを見たような顔で、ずっとずっと眺めていた。

She watched him.

For no reason, until the sun went down.

Wondering whether any of it had meaning.

She watched and watched, wearing the expression of someone who had been betrayed—or perhaps someone who had witnessed something precious.

どこにでもある放課後の出来事。

かすかに。
己にも見覚えのある、遠い日の風景だった。

That is the entire story.

An after-school incident of the most ordinary kind.

But for her, it was a formative scene—something close to a revolution.

—Faintly—

it was also a scene from long ago that I myself remembered.

pages.ja:

世界は完全に戻っていく。

片腕に異物を迎えたまま、内側から切り離された。

The world restores itself completely.

My consciousness, folded into something narrow and therefore strong, evaporates with terrifying speed.

Like a bubble vanishing upon the surface of the sea.

With foreign matter welcomed into one arm, I am severed from the inner world.
